To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the accuracy of simple initials-based methods for disambiguating author names is sufficient for a number of important purposes, (2) the accuracy can be further improved by using an additional, simple, method, and (3) there is little to be gained from more sophisticated methods that use co-authorship patterns or other advanced features.

(i) the first initial method is already very accurate (97% correct) and is sufficient for many purposes, (ii) the second initial method, which is less accurate, is still useful for certain datasets and (iii) a simple method that combines the first initial and all initial methods, and implicitly takes into account the last-name frequency and the size dataset, is the most effective and can reduce the number of incorrectly identified authors up to 30%.
